title: Guide: batches and restarts
description: A search of A that blocks wrong candidates and collects their counterexamples; after 10 it restarts and adds the clauses the check wrote with clause/3. See the guide page "Loop shapes".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The Paley graph on n nodes (n a prime of the form 4m + 1): two nodes are joined when
% their difference is a square modulo n.
node(0..n-1).
square((X*X) \ n) :- X = 1..n-1.
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V, square((V-U) \ n).
fragments.description: The Paley graph on n nodes. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: c nodes that are not deleted and pairwise joined.
c { q(V) : node(V) } c.
:- q(V), del(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
#show q/1.

% One clause: one of the clique's nodes must be deleted.
clause(1, del(V), true) :- q(V).
fragments.description: Looks for a surviving clique and writes the clause with clause/3 (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Search, collect the counterexamples, restart after 10, and add their clauses
# (written by the check with clause/3) between two searches.
pending = []
repeat:
    search A:
        on candidate M:
            X = C.solve(assume G(M))
            if X:
                pending.push(X)
                reject M with G.block(M)
                if pending.size >= 10: restart
    added = pending.size
    for X in pending:
        A.add(G.clauses(X))
    pending.clear()
until A.exhausted and added == 0
